title: Normalized constant-to-integral coefficient square and flat K-flat pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On the small pro-étale sites put $C_Z=(A)_Z$, $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ and $S_{n,Z}=(A/\pi^n)_Z$ for $Z=X,Y$, $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $i_Z:C_Z\to R_Z$ for the constant-function map, $r_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{i_Z}$ for scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $g_R^*,g_C^*$ for module pullback along the canonical coefficient maps [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms].

The canonical projections identify $R_Z\cong\varprojlim_n S_{n,Z}$ as ring sheaves, $R_Z$ is flat over $C_Z$, and $R_Z/\pi^nR_Z\cong S_{n,Z}$ with the prescribed quotient projections. Put $a_C:g^{-1}C_Y\cong C_X$ and $a_R:g^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$ for the canonical coefficient identifications. Then
$$a_R\,g^{-1}i_Y=i_Xa_C.$$
For every (possibly unbounded) cochain complex $H$ of $R_Y$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$d_H:r_Xg_R^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}g_C^*r_YH.$$
Its underlying abelian-sheaf map is the identity after both sides are identified with $g^{-1}H$: the completed scalar-extension identification sends $r\otimes h$ to $a_R^{-1}(r)h$ and its inverse sends $h$ to $1\otimes h$, with the analogous formulas over $C$. These identifications agree on the $C_X$-actions and specify $d_H$ on all scalar-extension generators. Both module pullbacks are exact. If $P$ is K-flat with flat terms over $R_Y$, then $r_YP$, $g_R^*P$, and $g_C^*r_YP$ are K-flat with flat terms over $C_Y,R_X,C_X$, respectively [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No boundedness, constructibility or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $H$ or $P$.

proof.text: Use the integral assertion of admissible scalar realization for the spectral topology on O_E. The DVR uniformizer generates its maximal ideal. Its completed identification supplies the ring-sheaf isomorphism and exactly the constant-scalar residue normalization on X and Y.

For a Noetherian completed constant ring, each projection is surjective on sections and its kernel is generated locally by the constant ideal power. Apply the proved projection-surjectivity-and-kernel part of the completed constant algebra theorem. A compatible ring map annihilates that kernel by its linear version, and therefore factors uniquely through the projection. The factors are natural, giving the specified pushout of ring sheaves. Transport the pushout across the normalized completed identification. Exact internal scalar extension identifies, after forgetting, with tensoring by the restricted regular module. Since forgetting reflects finite limits, the restricted regular module is internally flat; the section tensor comparison makes it flat on the site.

Apply naturality of upperStarFromPointComp to the discrete-to-continuous scalar map. This is precisely the scalar square. Cancel the invertible coefficient comparisons to obtain the inverse square. Use the extension-along-isomorphism quotient formula to prove both generator formulas for each coefficient ring.

Whisker the Cartesian pullback isomorphism with scalar restriction. Between the two inverse-image lifts use the change-of-scalars-square isomorphism, whose underlying map is the identity, then the inverse Cartesian comparison. Cancellation gives the required normalization. Apply mapHomologicalComplex to this natural isomorphism; it is the required whole-chain comparison in every integer degree. The existing exactness instances give both exactFunctor assertions.

Encode scalar restriction as sectionwise restriction using the canonical sectionModuleComapIso and identify the regular module with the unit. Its established flatness is the hypothesis of flat scalar restriction preserving K-flatness. Transport K-flatness and termwise flatness through the same comparison, using invariance under isomorphism.

The canonical Cartesian comparison identifies module pullback with inverse image followed by restriction along the inverse coefficient isomorphism. This preserves flat objects by the proved inverse-image flatness theorem. The section tensor comparison equates the recorded K-flatness test with internal K-flatness; the latter is equivalently the K-flat homotopy-category predicate. Apply the generic theorem that a flat-preserving additive colimit functor sends K-flat complexes with flat terms to K-flat complexes, and translate back. Apply this first to P and then to its scalar restriction. This includes unbounded complexes.

proof_origin.place: Y8 Lean proof: normalized completed identification and flatness via admissible scalar realization; ring quotient pushout from the completed-constant kernel theorem; canonical scalar naturality and extension-along-isomorphism generator formulas; termwise comparison; flat restriction and the generic flat-term K-flat functor theorem applied to module inverse image.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q111-c8b58a958 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no changes. The delivery splits the item into 8 steps with no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. On the base the item was unsplit with no proof, no repair note exists, and it is not on a dropped list. Its only citer, lem-sfb-integral-pullback-strict-roos-normalization (O3), uses exactly the clauses it states, and the proof dependencies form no cycle. Sources read: blueprint det-lem-int-tensor-pullback, its first paragraph and the 'Comparison with the Stacks Project' paragraph; Stacks Tag 093M (sites-modules l.8261) and Tag 0G7E (sites-cohomology l.3508); Lean FiniteConstantModelResolution.lean:131-147, where scalarToContinuous is the sheafified constant-function map on Profinite. Step 1: the hypotheses of the compact-adic identification hold (compact Hausdorff domain, finite A/π^{n+1}, and the q_{n+1}-fibre basis from coset-basis), and the scalar-to-residue projections follow without commuting inverse image with a limit. Step 2: Noetherian O_E plus the completed-constant node with S=R_Z and c=i_Z gives flatness; the quotient clause at index n-1 gives R/π^nR ≅ S_n, and the explicit inverses check out (π^n s⊗1=0). Step 3: the square follows from naturality of α_g at the discrete-to-adic map j, with i_Z=p_Z^*(j)∘κ_Z. Identifying α at A_disc with a_C rests on both maps sending the constant scalar a to a. This short coherence is acceptable as an elementary step. Uniqueness alone would not be enough, because O_E can have nontrivial ring automorphisms, but the step argues through the scalar-preserving property. Steps 4-5: I checked the balancing and the two inverse maps; the C_X-actions agree by the square, and naturality and compatibility with differentials hold for unbounded complexes. Step 6: g_R^* is exact by the Cartesian-coefficients node; for g_C^* the underlying functor is g^{-1}, and the lem-pe constant-scalar lift covers any ring. Steps 7-8: flat scalar restriction preserves K-flatness, and the ringed-topos pullback lemma (= Stacks 0G7E) is applied twice with the correct inputs; no boundedness is needed. Edge cases g=id, n=1, X=∅ and the zero complex are fine. I accept the 9 generic tool_uses (coefficient, flatness and K-flat tools from other units); unit sk-lem-int-tensor has no node of its own for them. No SGA source and no direct trf citation.
